training_data: Shanghai Memory Study (memory clinic of Huashan Hospital, Fudan University, Shanghai): 116 MCI (41 converters/75 non-converters); features selected by group t-tests on the whole cohort, SVM evaluated by stratified 10-fold CV
test_data: ADNI 1/2/GO: 102 MCI (25 converters/77 non-converters); the SMS-selected features were carried over, but the SVM was rebuilt and evaluated by 10-fold CV within ADNI (sMRI+fMRI AUC 0.86)
reason: Only the feature set was transferred to ADNI: the SVM was re-trained ('tuned') on ADNI data and scored by 10-fold cross-validation there, so ADNI took part in developing the model it evaluates and this is not V4. Within each cohort the design is k-fold CV without a held-out partition, which is V2; V1 (LOOCV) is also wrong.

quotes.quote: Two independent cohorts were used: Shanghai Memory Study (SMS) cohort for selection of potentially effective features and internal cross-validation, and ADNI cohort for these features' external validation, which is different from SMS cohort in population origins, clinical characteristics, scanners, and imaging parameters.

The same MCI features for MCI prediction selected by SMS cohort were applied to ADNI cohort, to evaluate the effectiveness of these selected features on an independent external dataset. SVM-based prediction model construction and evaluation, and the 10-fold cross-validation approach was also utilized in ADNI data, in consistency with SMS cohort.
Specifically, the models constructed from SMS cohort were tuned when validated on ADNI cohort, using same selected MRI predictors as inputs.

Given these factors in nature, it is plausible to tune the neuroimaging models to obtain population-specific parameters for the selected MRI predictors, which alleviate the influence of population heterogeneity and contribute to the effectiveness of proposed imaging features.
